subject: Order Form + Pricing Appendix — reconciliation of caps/floors and packaging credits
messages:
From: AceroHealth Procurement <procurement@acerohealth.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acerohealth.com
Date: Wed, 09 Apr 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form + Pricing Appendix — redline questions

Hi David —

Thanks for sending the draft order form. We reviewed the Pricing Appendix and attached a marked-up PDF (Acero_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) with a few open questions before we route to finance for approval: 

1) Floor / Minimums: the current Exhibit B references an annualized minimum that seems to double-count monthly true-ups with the quarterly true-up language. Can you confirm which mechanism governs true-ups (monthly vs quarterly)? We need clarity for our forecasting.

2) Cap smoothing: the cap language appears to allow a mid-year bucket reallocation but doesn’t specify how leftover committed tokens are reconciled on early termination. Is there an earnback or pro-rata refund?

3) Packaging credit: the order includes a one-time packaging credit that your Pricing team labeled as a ‘transition credit’. Acero will need the credit to be treated as a credit against first invoice (not a separate refund liability). Can you confirm how Redwood will surface this on the invoice and in order schedule?

4) Revenue recognition / seat changes: if our usage spikes above the committed slab for 60 days, does the charge immediately migrate to the next slab or is a smoothing/true-up performed at quarter end?

Please see inline notes in the attached PDF and the spreadsheet (pricing_appendix_lineitem.xlsx) with our suggested numeric reconciliations. We’d like to get this finalized by next Monday (4/14) to keep the renewal timeline intact.

--
Sharon Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
AceroHealth
procurement@acerohealth.com

Attachments: Acero_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf), pricing_appendix_lineitem.xlsx (xlsx)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: AceroHealth Procurement <procurement@acerohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Apr 2025 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form + Pricing Appendix — reconciliation of caps/floors and packaging credits

Hi Sharon —

Appreciate the detailed pass — good catch on the overlapping true-up language. Quick summary of our position and proposed edits: 

- True-up cadence: our intent was quarterly true-ups (end-of-quarter reconciliation). The monthly reference slipped in during an earlier draft and should be removed. We propose replacing the monthly language with an explicit quarterly true-up clause and a short definition for "Billing Period".

- Early termination / leftover commit: we can offer an earnback credit for the unused portion on early termination if termination is for convenience after the first 12 months. The amount would be prorated based on remaining committed tokens less applied usage credits; we suggest adding a 90‑day notice exception for force majeure.

- Packaging credit: we can confirm the transition credit will be applied as a credit on Acero's first invoice. We'll add language to the Order Schedule that the credit will appear as a line item labeled "Transition Credit - Order ACERO-2309" and reduce the first invoice amount accordingly.

- Smoothing on slab spikes: usage over a slab will be charged at overage rates in real time; however, for committed slab movement we can allow a one-time mid-quarter adjustment if the increased volume is sustained for 60+ days, with the charge formalized at the subsequent quarterly true-up. This keeps latency low while avoiding surprise monthly reclassification.

I've attached a one-page summary (dk_redline_summary.pdf) with proposed clause text. Jordan — can you review the suggested legal language for Exhibit B and confirm whether the earnback phrasing is acceptably firm or too operational? Marissa — can you confirm the invoicing format with finance and whether applying the transition credit against the first invoice has any billing system constraints?

If that sounds acceptable, we'll circulate a tracked-change clean-up and get it back to you by Friday so Legal can sign off before the April 14th deadline.

Thanks,

David Kim
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: dk_redline_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form + Pricing Appendix — reconciliation of caps/floors and packaging credits

David / Marissa —

Quick legal pass below (trackable edits to follow):

- Quarterly true-up: accept. Replace the "monthly" reference with "quarterly" and define "Billing Period" to avoid ambiguity. Also add an example table in Exhibit B to show how a quarter true-up would flow (example numbers keep operational disputes low).

- Early termination earnback: recommend limiting earnback to 50% of the remaining committed net of any used tokens to balance customer goodwill and revenue protection. Also include a cure period for material breach. Proposed snippet: "In the event of Customer termination for convenience after twelve (12) months, Redwood will credit fifty percent (50%) of the pro rata remaining committed fees, net of usage credits, subject to Customer's satisfaction of outstanding payment obligations."

- Packaging credit: legal is fine with it being on first invoice; include sentence that the credit is non-refundable and must be applied within first billing cycle. That prevents later accounting disputes.

- Mid-quarter slab movement: allow one operational reclassification per fiscal year unless otherwise agreed in writing. This prevents repeated gaming while providing flexibility.

Also flag: ensure the Order Schedule includes a single source-of-truth table (appendix) for rate card IDs and mapping to slab definitions. Without that the spreadsheet will become the defacto contract and create mismatch risk.

I'll send a tracked-change markup to David's PDF and to the Excel by EOD.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
jordan_blake@redwood.com

2) On the earnback: Acero can accept a 50% earnback but requests an explicit exclusion for termination due to Redwood's material breach.

If you can produce a cleaned, tracked-change Order Form with those two clarifications, we can circulate internally and get to countersignature. Also please send a DocuSign envelope with the final Order Form + Exhibit B when ready — procurement will approve quickly once the document is clean.
